newsitem.title: FRANCE: French dailies earn strong Q1 ad income-Liberation.
newsitem.headline: French dailies earn strong Q1 ad income-Liberation.

text.p: French newspapers had strong advertising income in the first quarter of 1997 and dailies Liberation, Le Monde and La Tribune fared better than the average newspaper, a top executive at Liberation said.

Evence-Charles Coppee, Liberation's managing director, told a journalists' briefing on Wednesday that his newspaper's net advertising income in the four months to end-April was nine percent higher than in the same period of 1996.
"In the first quarter of 1997 the advertising market was good and Liberation, Le Monde and La Tribune reacted better than the market," he said.
Liberation had advertising revenue of 92.2 million francs ($15.8 million) for the whole of 1996.
Coppee said Liberation should make a profit in 1997 after showing a net attributable loss of 27.7 million francs in 1996 on turnover of 435.6 million francs.
Its total circulation rose 2.4 percent to an average of 162,300 copies a day in the five months to end-May compared with the same period a yeaer earlier, he said.
Liberation's parent company, SAIP, is 65 percent owned by France's Chargeurs. DT/SLA ($ = 5.821 French Francs)
